question: What often happens when patients simply cannot afford the high cost of their prescribed medications?

options.A: Pharmacies are forced to give all drugs away
options.B: They may skip doses or stop taking them
options.C: Hospital admissions instantly drop to zero
options.D: They automatically receive free government refills

explanation: Exactly. When out-of-pocket costs are too high, patients often try to stretch their drugs by skipping doses, which delays their healing.

question: What major organ side effect must nurses watch out for when patients take drugs like isoniazid and rifampicin?

options.A: Liver toxicity or hepatotoxicity
options.B: Sudden bone fractures
options.C: Permanent kidney failure
options.D: Complete hair loss

explanation: First-line TB drugs are processed by the liver, so nurses must monitor closely for signs of liver stress or toxicity.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to good teamwork?

options.A: Professional rivalry
options.B: Open communication channels
options.C: Lack of time
options.D: Unclear hierarchies

explanation: Correct! Open communication helps a team thrive—it's definitely not a barrier!

question: How does simple handwashing with soap directly help prevent illness in a community?

options.A: It alters the chemical composition of drinking water to kill harmful bacteria
options.B: It stimulates the bone marrow to produce millions of new red blood cells daily
options.C: It removes transient pathogens from the hands, preventing them from entering the body
options.D: It permanently neutralizes airborne droplets before they reach the respiratory tract

explanation: You nailed it! Our hands pick up germs everywhere; washing them washes away those hitchhiking pathogens before they can get into our mouths, noses, or eyes.

question: Why might a nursing student take a beta-blocker like propranolol before giving a major class presentation?

options.A: To increase their energy levels and stage presence
options.B: To cure their underlying social phobia permanently
options.C: To prevent them from falling asleep during the performance
options.D: To control physical symptoms like a racing heart and tremors

explanation: Beta-blockers block adrenaline, keeping your hands steady and heart calm without making your mind foggy. A real lifesaver for stage fright!

question: Which heart rhythm do adults in sudden cardiac arrest show most often?

options.A: Atrial flutter
options.B: First-degree heart block
options.C: Ventricular fibrillation
options.D: Sinus bradycardia

explanation: In ventricular fibrillation, the lower chambers just quiver uselessly instead of pumping. Recognizing this rhythm is a key nursing skill!

question: What is the main action to take when a patient is in Asystole?

options.A: Apply transcutaneous pacing pads immediately
options.B: Perform high-quality CPR and give epinephrine without shocking
options.C: Deliver an immediate high-energy defibrillation shock
options.D: Stop all resuscitation efforts because the patient cannot be saved

explanation: Asystole is a flat line with no electrical signal to reset, so shocks will not help; CPR and drugs are needed. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the single biggest cause of cancer worldwide that we can actually prevent?

options.A: Processed meat intake
options.B: Alcohol consumption
options.C: Ultraviolet radiation
options.D: Tobacco use

explanation: Tobacco smoke contains harmful chemicals that damage our DNA. Avoiding tobacco is one of the best health choices anyone can make!

question: How did Nigerian mothers traditionally space their children before modern contraceptives arrived?

options.A: Daily ingestion of synthetic hormone pills
options.B: Intrauterine copper device insertion
options.C: Surgical tubal ligation procedures
options.D: Prolonged breastfeeding and postpartum abstinence

explanation: Traditional Nigerian societies used natural, reliable spacing methods like extended breastfeeding and resting from sex after childbirth.

question: Why do we usually avoid estrogen-containing pills for mothers who are breastfeeding?

options.A: They can significantly reduce the breast milk supply
options.B: They transfer directly into breast milk as a heavy poison
options.C: They stimulate excessive and painful uterine contractions
options.D: They always cause immediate cessation of all lochia

explanation: Estrogen can lower milk volume. That is why progestin-only options or non-hormonal methods are much safer choices for nursing mums early on.

question: What is the very first step in the community mobilisation process?

options.A: Building a permanent hospital
options.B: Evaluating project funds
options.C: Mass immunisation
options.D: Entry and sensitization

explanation: Before doing anything else, health workers must properly introduce themselves and gain entry through appropriate community channels. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h5)

question: How should an airport security check be handled for a passenger with a pacemaker?

options.A: Turn off the pacemaker completely using an external switch before entering the security line
options.B: Walk through the metal detector normally, but ask security to avoid using a hand-held wand over the chest
options.C: Show the medical card and demand a full body cavity search instead of walking through arches
options.D: Refuse all security screening because airport machines will instantly destroy the pacemaker

explanation: Walking through the security arch is usually fine if you keep moving, but security should avoid holding a magnetic wand directly over the chest. Practical knowledge for clinical practice!

question: Which ethical principle gives a patient the right to make their own food choices?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Justice
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Spot on! Autonomy is all about self-determination—respecting that patients have the final say over their own bodies and choices. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h2)

question: When a patient has tummy pain, asking what makes the pain better or worse helps you figure out what?

options.A: The patient's family history of illness
options.B: The patient's surgical background
options.C: The exact medical diagnosis of the disease
options.D: Relieving and aggravating factors

explanation: Spot on! Finding out what triggers or soothes the pain helps you identify its relieving and aggravating factors.

question: Which personal trait helps a nurse leader bounce back quickly from tough ward stresses?

options.A: Compliance
options.B: Rigidity
options.C: Resilience
options.D: Aloofness

explanation: Resilience is your inner strength. It's what helps you keep your cool and bounce back after dealing with a really difficult shift or unexpected workplace stress.

question: A farmer arrives at the clinic with severe muscle twitching and too much saliva after working in the fields. What caused this?

options.A: A natural disaster caused by flooding
options.B: A chemical exposure from pesticides
options.C: A traumatic injury from a falling tree branch
options.D: A biological outbreak of meningitis

explanation: Pesticides are powerful chemicals that affect the nervous system, leading to symptoms like twitching and excess saliva. You're learning fast!

question: A patient has a breathing rate of 32 breaths per minute and an oxygen level of 91% on room air. How is this classified?

options.A: Asymptomatic infection
options.B: Mild illness
options.C: Severe illness
options.D: Moderate illness

explanation: An oxygen level below 94% along with fast breathing means the patient is struggling and needs urgent care. You can totally master this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h3)

question: Which clinical measurement is used during routine clinic visits to monitor physical fetal growth?

options.A: Fundal height in centimeters
options.B: Maternal weight gain in pounds
options.C: Fetal movement count per hour
options.D: Abdominal girth around the navel

explanation: Measuring fundal height (from the pubic bone to the top of the uterus) gives us a quick, reliable way to check that the baby is growing nicely week by week.

question: What crucial instruction should a nurse give to a pregnant woman diagnosed with a low-lying placenta (placenta praevia)?

options.A: Take iron supplements only when bleeding starts
options.B: Restrict fluid intake to prevent swelling
options.C: Avoid sexual intercourse in late pregnancy
options.D: Engage in heavy daily aerobic exercise

explanation: Avoiding activities that can disturb the lower uterine segment, such as sexual intercourse, helps prevent triggering sudden bleeding when the placenta is low. Simple and life-saving!

question: Which level of prevention uses routine immunizations to stop a disease before it even starts?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention is all about stopping health problems before they begin—vaccines are a classic example. Brilliant work!

question: What is the main focus of Psychological First Aid (PFA) in a disaster?

options.A: Providing humane practical support and reducing distress
options.B: Conducting formal psychoanalysis sessions
options.C: Prescribing strong antidepressant medications
options.D: Diagnosing deep psychiatric disorders

explanation: Well done! PFA isn't about heavy therapy or psychoanalysis; it's about being human, offering practical comfort, and helping people feel safe.

question: How do governments use healthcare spending as a percentage of GDP?

options.A: To calculate individual patient prescription costs
options.B: To set the daily working hours for hospital staff
options.C: To determine the required passing grade for nursing students
options.D: To measure how much national wealth goes toward medical care

explanation: This ratio shows the proportion of a country's total economic output dedicated to keeping people healthy and running health services.

question: How is a dilator different from a regular feeding tube?

options.A: A dilator is specifically designed to stretch tight strictures.
options.B: A dilator is only used for temporary fluid drainage.
options.C: A feeding tube contains a built-in cutting blade.
options.D: A feeding tube is rigid while dilators are always soft.

explanation: While feeding tubes are for giving food, dilators are specially sized and shaped to gently stretch out narrowed tubes in the body.

question: Why is keeping patients in prolonged physical restraints at some spiritual healing camps a major concern?

options.A: It violates human rights and increases psychological trauma
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never feel sad again
options.C: It ensures the patient takes all necessary modern vitamins
options.D: It speeds up the healing process of brain tissues

explanation: Spot on! Chaining or locking up vulnerable individuals causes physical harm, deepens distress, and violates basic human rights.

question: Which blood vessels send branches to supply the ureters?

options.A: Femoral and popliteal arteries
options.B: Pulmonary and bronchial arteries
options.C: Renal and gonadal arteries
options.D: Coronary and carotid arteries

explanation: Nice effort! The ureters receive a rich blood supply from nearby neighbors like the renal and gonadal arteries.

question: What is the main focus of a healthcare manager compared to a leader?

options.A: Challenging outdated organizational traditions
options.B: Pioneering brand new clinical care models
options.C: Inspiring staff through a grand vision for the future
options.D: Maintaining daily operations and managing budgets

explanation: While leaders inspire and look ahead, managers focus on the day-to-day running of the ward, like making duty rosters and managing supplies.

question: A pregnant patient at 32 weeks says she hasn't felt her baby kick all day. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Advise her to wait until the next scheduled appointment next month
options.B: Arrange for an immediate assessment of fetal heart sounds and movement
options.C: Give her a strong laxative to stimulate digestive activity
options.D: Tell her this is completely normal and send her back home

explanation: Spot on! A quiet baby can mean distress. Always check fetal heartbeats and movements right away when a mum reports this.

question: Why is HIV disclosure considered a complex process for many patients?

options.A: It often involves heavy emotional strain and fear of social stigma
options.B: It is illegal in most healthcare jurisdictions without a judge's order
options.C: It requires advanced surgical training to explain to partners
options.D: It permanently stops the transmission of all other viral infections

explanation: Fear of rejection, discrimination, and violence makes sharing an HIV-positive status very difficult for many individuals. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h1)

question: Which ethical idea often guides a nurse when supplies run low during a massive disaster?

options.A: Absolute patient autonomy in demanding any available hospital bed
options.B: Strict non-maleficence without regard for community supply limits
options.C: Absolute paternalism where the nurse makes all household choices
options.D: Utilitarianism, focusing on the greatest good for the greatest number

explanation: When resources are scarce, disaster ethics leans toward helping the maximum number of survivors possible.

question: What key feature is missing in a quasi-experimental design that you would find in a true experiment?

options.A: Random assignment of participants
options.B: An independent variable
options.C: Measurement tools
options.D: Any form of clinical intervention

explanation: Quasi-experiments test interventions and compare groups, but they skip random assignment because it's often not practical in real hospitals.

question: Why might a patient with severe carbon monoxide poisoning show a falsely normal or high oxygen saturation reading on a pulse oximeter?

options.A: Carbon monoxide makes the pulse rate extremely fast
options.B: Cold fingers stop the machine from recording low numbers
options.C: Bright lights in the room interfere with the infrared sensors
options.D: The device reads carbon monoxide attached to hemoglobin just like oxygen

explanation: Standard pulse oximeters cannot distinguish between oxygen and carbon monoxide bound to hemoglobin, leading to dangerously misleading high readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h7)

question: What does an operating budget typically cover for a nursing unit?

options.A: The purchase of brand new hospital buildings and elevators
options.B: Emergency funds kept strictly for natural disasters
options.C: Long-term investments in overseas stock markets
options.D: Day-to-day expenses like staff salaries and routine medical supplies

explanation: Think of the operating budget as the money that pays for everyday running costs, like paying staff and buying routine ward supplies.

question: What is the biggest risk when a country relies heavily on foreign donor funding for healthcare?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take modern medications
options.B: The government will collect too much tax revenue locally
options.C: Programs may collapse if donor priorities or foreign policies change
options.D: Hospitals will automatically stop accepting local currency

explanation: Foreign aid can be unpredictable. If donors suddenly change their minds or pack up and leave, local health programs can fall apart if there's no backup plan.

question: What do we call the emotional exhaustion and stress health workers feel from constantly hearing trauma stories?

options.A: Compassion fatigue
options.B: Somatic conversion
options.C: Cognitive dissonance
options.D: Bipolar depression

explanation: Caring for others takes a toll. Compassion fatigue happens when nurses absorb too much of their patients' heavy suffering without enough time to recharge.

question: What is the main reason we calculate a patient's Body Mass Index (BMI)?

options.A: Determining daily fluid requirements
options.B: Screening for underweight, overweight, or obesity
options.C: Assessing cardiovascular fitness capacity
options.D: Measuring exact blood glucose levels

explanation: BMI is a quick way to use height and weight to check if a patient is carrying too much or too little weight.

question: What is the key difference between Acute Stress Disorder and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder?

options.A: Whether the patient has physical injuries or not
options.B: The time frame and duration of the symptoms
options.C: The age of the person experiencing the trauma
options.D: The specific type of disaster that caused the trauma

explanation: Acute Stress Disorder happens shortly after the event, whereas PTSD involves long-lasting symptoms that persist over months or years. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h3)

question: How does Staphylococcus aureus usually contaminate prepared foods like egg salads?

options.A: Prolonged exposure to direct sunlight
options.B: Direct handling by an infected food preparer
options.C: Absorption from contaminated soil during growth
options.D: Cross-contamination from raw root vegetables

explanation: Staph bacteria live naturally on our skin. If a food handler doesn't wash up well, the bacteria can easily transfer straight into the food during prep.

question: Why do theatres carefully monitor room temperature and humidity during surgery?

options.A: To make the room comfortable for visitors and family members
options.B: To ensure surgical instruments do not rust during the procedure
options.C: To discourage bacterial growth and prevent patient hypothermia
options.D: To keep the anesthesia machine running at peak efficiency

explanation: Controlling the climate stops bacteria from multiplying and protects the patient's body heat while they are under anesthesia. You've got this!

question: A patient with infrequent periods also has extra facial hair growth and bad acne. Which lab test is most important here?

options.A: Serum testosterone levels
options.B: Liver enzyme blood screen
options.C: Fast protein blood test
options.D: Urinary electrolyte panel

explanation: You're doing great! Extra hair growth and acne are signs of high androgens (male-type hormones), so checking testosterone levels helps point you right toward the diagnosis.

question: What can happen to patients when there is too much unwanted clinical variation?

options.A: Standardized pain control across all medical and surgical wards
options.B: Immediate reduction in total hospital operational expenses
options.C: Guaranteed faster recovery from complex surgical procedures
options.D: Increased risk of medical errors and longer hospital stays

explanation: You got it! When care is unpredictable and inconsistent, mistakes happen more easily, leading to longer stays for our patients.

question: Why do indwelling urinary catheters make a patient much more vulnerable to infections?

options.A: They make it impossible to clean the perineal area
options.B: They alter the body's natural hormone balance
options.C: They force the kidneys to produce toxic urine
options.D: They create an open pathway for bacteria to enter the bladder

explanation: That's right! The catheter tubing bypasses the body's natural defenses, giving bacteria a straight highway right into the sterile urinary tract.

question: Where would you most likely give general health guidance to a group of people?

options.A: An isolated psychiatric ward
options.B: A crowded clinic waiting room
options.C: An intensive care unit bedside
options.D: A private, locked therapy room

explanation: Guidance is often broad and preventive. A busy clinic waiting room is a classic spot to share health tips with groups!

question: What happens to a health facility if DRF medicines are priced way too low?

options.A: The facility will experience severe drug stock-outs
options.B: Private pharmacies will close down due to competition
options.C: The government will increase funding immediately
options.D: The pharmacy will accumulate excessive cash reserves

explanation: Makes sense, right? If you sell medicines below what it costs to buy them, the money runs out, and soon there are simply no drugs left on the pharmacy shelves for patients.

question: What is the main goal of quality assurance in nursing?

options.A: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment
options.B: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors
options.C: Preventing mistakes and monitoring care delivery
options.D: Increasing the number of daily patient admissions

explanation: You've got this! Quality assurance is all about being proactive—catching issues early and stopping harm before it even reaches the patient. Great nursing is about prevention!

question: What is the main focus of a national nursing organization like NANNM?

options.A: Country-specific labor laws and domestic health policies
options.B: Directing medical research for pharmaceutical corporations
options.C: Global monetary funds for hospital construction worldwide
options.D: Setting international travel guidelines for nurse migration

explanation: National bodies focus right at home—handling local working conditions, salaries, and health policies that directly affect nurses in our country.

question: What is the big giveaway that a study is non-experimental?

options.A: The researcher does not manipulate any variables
options.B: Participants are randomly assigned to a treatment
options.C: A new drug is tested on a control group
options.D: Data is collected exclusively through interviews

explanation: Correct! In non-experimental studies, you just observe what is happening naturally without changing or meddling with anything.

question: What exactly are 'Pick bodies' seen under a microscope in brain tissue?

options.A: Scars from previous traumatic head injuries
options.B: Deposits of calcium in the brain blood vessels
options.C: Clumps of abnormal tau protein inside nerve cells
options.D: Infections caused by bacteria in the spinal fluid

explanation: Pick bodies are just microscopic clumps of tangled tau protein. When neurons get weighed down by these clumps, they start to struggle and break down.

question: Which of these is a common everyday community stressor in our environment?

options.A: Living in a quiet, peaceful neighborhood
options.B: A balanced diet and regular exercise
options.C: Having too much free time and rest
options.D: Financial instability and high cost of living

explanation: Economic worries and the daily struggle to meet basic needs are massive sources of stress for many people around us.

question: A student nurse notices patients often get confused when discharged without written instructions. Why is this a valid research problem?

options.A: It highlights a communication gap that affects patient safety and outcomes
options.B: It proves that patients are entirely at fault for forgetting instructions
options.C: It shows that written paper is more expensive than digital tablets
options.D: It demonstrates that discharge rounds are unnecessary tasks

explanation: Discharge confusion puts patient recovery at risk. Studying how to fix this communication gap is super important for safe nursing!

question: Why is maintaining strict confidentiality regarding family planning crucial in community nursing?

options.A: To prevent the clinic from keeping accurate statistical records
options.B: To ensure that contraceptives are sold at higher market prices
options.C: To protect clients from social stigma and domestic conflict
options.D: To hide the nurse's activities from local government leaders

explanation: Clients may face backlash or relationship issues if their contraceptive choices are shared without permission in tight-knit communities. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h8)

question: What is the main goal of nursing research?

options.A: To reduce the number of working hours for staff
options.B: To develop trustworthy knowledge for the profession
options.C: To replace doctors in making medical diagnoses
options.D: To eliminate the need for clinical experience

explanation: Spot on! Nursing research is all about building a solid foundation of proven facts to make patient care better across the board. You've got this!

question: Why are anticholinergic drugs sometimes given to patients right before surgery?

options.A: To reduce oral and respiratory secretions
options.B: To lower the patient's blood pressure
options.C: To completely paralyze skeletal muscles
options.D: To induce deep general anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Drying up spit and mucus helps keep the airway clear and stops fluid from getting into the lungs during surgery.

question: What must a nurse do when they suspect an older adult is being abused at home?

options.A: Keep the information strictly confidential to protect family trust
options.B: Report the suspicion to the designated protective services authority
options.C: Wait until absolute proof is gathered before telling anyone else
options.D: Advise the patient to handle the situation independently

explanation: Nurses are mandatory reporters! You don't need absolute proof to report—just reasonable suspicion to keep your patient safe.

question: What is a transitional enclave model in sheltered employment?

options.A: A small group working inside a regular business with a job coach
options.B: A workshop that only operates during the night shift
options.C: A factory run entirely by robotic machines without humans
options.D: An online virtual office where clients work from home

explanation: An enclave places clients right inside a normal workplace while giving them the safety net of special supervision. You're crushing your studies!

question: Why is prevalence data most useful for community health nurses?

options.A: It proves the exact day a patient contracted an illness
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical diagnosis in the field
options.C: It stops new infections from entering the community
options.D: It helps plan long-term care and allocate resources

explanation: Knowing the total burden of disease helps nurses and health planners prepare adequate facilities and supplies. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which quick check do nurses use to spot life-threatening conditions in disaster victims first?

options.A: GCS neurological scale
options.B: Braden skin assessment
options.C: APGAR scoring system
options.D: ABCDE framework

explanation: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, and Exposure give us a fast, life-saving checklist in any emergency.

question: What is a primary immunodeficiency disorder?

options.A: Something that only affects adults over sixty
options.B: An issue triggered by common painkillers
options.C: An inherited genetic defect present right from birth
options.D: A condition caused by severe physical trauma later in life

explanation: Think of 'primary' as being born with it. These disorders stem from gene mutations passed down from parents, unlike secondary ones that happen later in life.

question: What are the three simple action steps in Psychological First Aid (PFA)?

options.A: Assess, Diagnose, and Treat
options.B: Observe, Intervene, and Evaluate
options.C: Search, Rescue, and Stabilize
options.D: Look, Listen, and Link

explanation: Easy to remember: Look for safety, Listen with empathy, and Link people to the help they need. You've got this!

question: Which document lists the minimum qualifications, training, and skills needed for a specific hospital job?

options.A: Incident report
options.B: Patient care plan
options.C: Job description
options.D: Job specification

explanation: A job specification spells out the 'specifications' or requirements of the person doing the job—like specific nursing qualifications and training needed.

question: What do we mean by the 'social determinants of health'?

options.A: The exact dosages of psychiatric prescription drugs
options.B: The specific genetic codes inherited from parents
options.C: The laboratory tests used to diagnose depression
options.D: The non-medical conditions where people live and work

explanation: Exactly! Things like where you sleep, how much you earn, and your access to school play a massive role in how healthy you are.

question: When is it best for a nurse researcher to choose a qualitative study design?

options.A: When measuring physical vital signs with a machine
options.B: When calculating exact drug dosages and blood levels
options.C: When comparing large statistical datasets of numbers
options.D: When exploring deep human experiences and meanings

explanation: Qualitative research is all about words, feelings, and personal stories. Use it when you want to understand *how* people feel or experience things.

question: What is a maladaptive coping mechanism?

options.A: A medical test used to check neurotransmitter levels
options.B: A healthy way of solving problems during a crisis
options.C: A strategy that makes stress harder to handle over time
options.D: A genetic trait passed down from parents to children

explanation: Maladaptive coping refers to unhealthy habits like avoidance or denial that provide temporary relief but worsen mental health in the long run. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of food hygiene and safety practices?

options.A: To ensure food is safe and wholesome for consumption
options.B: To make meals taste better and look colorful
options.C: To make cooking faster in large kitchens
options.D: To cut down the cost of buying ingredients

explanation: Food hygiene is all about stopping contamination so the food we eat stays safe and healthy from the farm or market straight to the table!

question: Which of the following is NOT a legal duty of a nurse handling controlled drugs?

options.A: Changing the doctor's prescription order to match ward supplies
options.B: Reporting missing medication from the drug cupboard
options.C: Verifying the patient's identity before administration
options.D: Documenting every dose given accurately

explanation: Nurses cannot alter prescriptions; doing so is illegal and falsifies medical records. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h5)

question: A community has non-English speakers and residents with hearing impairments. How should you adapt the emergency warning system?

options.A: Assume residents will translate the news for each other
options.B: Rely entirely on standard written flyers distributed in mailboxes
options.C: Broadcast warnings exclusively in the national official language
options.D: Provide multilingual materials and sign language interpreters

explanation: Spot on! Tailoring your messages to meet specific language and sensory needs ensures that no vulnerable group is left in the dark.

question: Why should a midwife check her emergency maternity bag on a regular weekly basis?

options.A: To ensure all liquid drugs are transferred into clear glass bottles
options.B: To verify that patient clinical notes are stored inside the drug kit
options.C: To catch expired medications and restock depleted emergency supplies
options.D: To clean the exterior leather surface with strong chemical bleach

explanation: You're thinking like a pro! Regular checks mean you'll never be caught off guard by expired drugs during an emergency.

question: What is often the earliest warning sign of endometrial cancer in women who have gone through menopause?

options.A: Abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Severe lower back pain
options.C: Rapid weight gain
options.D: Swollen lower extremities

explanation: Any spotting or bleeding after menopause is never normal and is usually the very first clue that prompts doctors to check the uterine lining.

question: Which of these is a key part of our fast-acting, innate immunity?

options.A: Phagocytosis by macrophages
options.B: Production of specific antibodies
options.C: Long-term memory cell creation
options.D: Delayed T-lymphocyte activation

explanation: Macrophages are like the body's cleanup crew. They use phagocytosis (swallowing up germs) as a quick, first-line defense against any invader.

question: What is entomology?

options.A: The study of parasitic worms and flukes
options.B: The analysis of fungal infections
options.C: The scientific study of insects
options.D: The clinical study of human blood cells

explanation: Entomology is specifically the branch of zoology that focuses on insects and their relationship with the environment and humans. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why do people on a strict plant-based diet need to mix different types of plant foods carefully?

options.A: Plants provide too much energy and cause rapid weight gain
options.B: Individual plant proteins are often missing some essential amino acids
options.C: Plant foods contain no vitamins or minerals whatsoever
options.D: Animal sources are the only legal foods allowed in clinical wards

explanation: Great thinking! Single plant foods usually lack one or two essential amino acids, so mixing beans and grains gives you a complete protein package.

question: What is the main idea behind performance-based financing in health aid?

options.A: Government budgets are approved without any review of previous hospital spending
options.B: Donors pay hospitals based on the total number of physical buildings they own
options.C: Funds are released only after verifying specific health service outcomes
options.D: Nurses receive salaries calculated solely on the number of hours they sleep on duty

explanation: With this approach, money is only released after seeing real, measurable results, like an increase in successful deliveries or immunizations.

question: Which lymphoid organ is primarily responsible for filtering blood and destroying old red blood cells?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Thymus
options.C: Liver
options.D: Tonsil

explanation: The spleen filters blood, recycles iron from hemoglobin, and removes damaged red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why are weekly feedback graphs posted on the staff notice board helpful?

options.A: They show nurses the tangible impact and results of their hard work
options.B: They prevent family members from visiting patients too often
options.C: They act as legal documents for the court if a patient sues
options.D: They replace the need for any verbal handovers between shifts

explanation: Seeing positive trends on a graph motivates the team to keep up their efforts and proves the new practice is working. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the main thing that sets a medical emergency apart from a trauma case?

options.A: It is always caused by a blunt or penetrating external force
options.B: It occurs exclusively in patients with a history of surgery
options.C: It develops slowly over several months without sudden changes
options.D: It arises from internal disease processes or system breakdown

explanation: Think of medical emergencies as coming from within—like an organ failure or sudden illness—while trauma comes from outside forces. You've got this!

question: Why do nurses place a waterproof pad under the patient during a wet compress procedure?

options.A: To anchor the patient firmly to the mattress
options.B: To increase the local therapeutic heat retention
options.C: To prevent moisture from soaking the bed linens
options.D: To block electrical currents from nearby wall outlets

explanation: Compresses are wet! A waterproof barrier keeps the patient's bed dry and keeps them comfortable.

question: What is the main job of mifepristone during a medical abortion?

options.A: Stimulating strong uterine contractions
options.B: Inducing systemic maternal hypertension
options.C: Blocking progesterone receptors to detach the sac
options.D: Paralyzing the musculature of the cervix

explanation: You've got this! Mifepristone blocks progesterone, the hormone needed to maintain pregnancy. This causes the uterine lining to soften and detaches the sac, preparing the way for the next step.

question: Why should a nurse avoid crushing an enteric-coated tablet?

options.A: It turns the solid pill into an unmixable powder
options.B: It changes the color of the liquid mixture
options.C: It causes the medication to dissolve too slowly
options.D: It ruins the special coating designed to protect the stomach

explanation: Enteric coatings protect the stomach lining from irritation or protect the drug from stomach acid; crushing destroys this barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h1)

question: What action should a nurse take immediately before leaving a computer workstation on the ward?

options.A: Lock or log out of the workstation to prevent unauthorized access
options.B: Minimize the patient charts without locking the screen
options.C: Turn off the main electrical power switch in the room
options.D: Leave the screen open for the next shift nurse

explanation: Locking unattended screens prevents unauthorized people from viewing confidential patient health records. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is a major operational headache for many voluntary health agencies?

options.A: Strict government bans on health education
options.B: Unstable and unpredictable funding sources
options.C: Zero demand for healthcare in rural areas
options.D: An excessive surplus of medical personnel

explanation: Spot on! Because they depend heavily on donations and grants, money can run out unexpectedly, making long-term planning tough.

question: What is the main difference between a human-made disaster and a natural disaster?

options.A: It always provides weeks of advance warning to the public
options.B: It is triggered by human actions or technical failures
options.C: It never results in mass casualties or physical injuries
options.D: It only occurs inside large industrial manufacturing factories

explanation: You've got this! Human-made disasters happen because of human errors, equipment failures, or negligence, rather than forces of nature like storms or earthquakes.

question: Where must the traction weight bags always be positioned?

options.A: Tied tightly to the metal headboard of the bed
options.B: Supported on a small stool placed next to the bed
options.C: Resting securely on the bottom mattress for safety
options.D: Hanging freely without touching the floor or bed frame

explanation: Spot on! If the weights rest on the floor, the pulling force stops, and the patient's neck bones could shift out of alignment.

question: What is the biggest health benefit of colostrum (the first breastmilk)?

options.A: It supplies excess fat calories to promote rapid weight gain
options.B: It provides high concentrations of protective antibodies and protein
options.C: It contains high levels of iron to prevent infant anemia
options.D: It acts as a strong laxative to prevent infantile jaundice

explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold for the baby! It's packed with antibodies that coat their tummy and protect their brand-new immune system against germs.

question: What is the physical cause of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)?

options.A: A bacterial infection destroying the tympanic membrane
options.B: Dislodged calcium crystals floating in the semicircular canals
options.C: Accumulation of cerumen deep in the inner ear canal
options.D: Chronic inflammation of the pharyngeal tonsils

explanation: Imagine tiny calcium crystals (otoconia) floating where they shouldn't be in your inner ear fluid. When you move your head, they drift and send dizzy, false motion signals to your brain!

question: A patient in the intensive care unit is being evaluated for potential brain death. Which test is routinely used to confirm this?

options.A: Electroencephalography
options.B: Lumbar puncture
options.C: Barium swallow study
options.D: Electromyography

explanation: When doctors need to check for remaining brain activity in severe cases, a completely flatline EEG (cerebral silence) helps confirm brain death.

question: What is the primary purpose of using orthopedic traction?

options.A: To apply a pulling force to align bones and reduce spasms
options.B: To completely immobilize the patient without using any bed sheets
options.C: To permanently replace damaged joint cartilage without surgery
options.D: To deliver strong local pain medication directly into a fracture

explanation: Traction uses a steady pull on body parts to restore bone alignment, stretch tight muscles, and ease painful spasms before definitive repair. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why should a nurse refer to the National Health Act when talking to health authorities about changes?

options.A: It exempts the nurse from paying professional licensing taxes
options.B: It gives legal backing and strength to the nurse's advocacy demands
options.C: It prevents patients from filing lawsuits against nurses
options.D: It allows the nurse to take over the duties of the hospital director

explanation: Exactly! Backing your points up with official health laws turns a simple complaint into a serious, legal expectation that administrators can't easily brush aside.

question: What are the three parts of the traditional epidemiological triad?

options.A: Bacteria, virus, and fungi
options.B: Patient, nurse, and doctor
options.C: Symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment
options.D: Agent, host, and environment

explanation: You will see this triad everywhere in public health! It looks at how the disease agent interacts with the vulnerable host (the person) and their surrounding environment.

question: What component of the epidemiological triangle refers to the external surroundings that allow a pathogen to thrive?

options.A: The susceptible host
options.B: The environment
options.C: The biological reservoir
options.D: The infectious agent

explanation: The environment represents external conditions and surroundings that facilitate the interaction between the host and the disease-causing agent. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is a major advantage of community-based mental health programs?

options.A: They completely remove the need for any professional medical staff
options.B: They require patients to live inside locked hospital facilities
options.C: They keep patients connected to their families and local neighborhoods
options.D: They eliminate all symptoms of mental illness permanently

explanation: Community-based care allows individuals to receive treatment while staying integrated in their daily social and family environments. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h7)

question: A male patient comes in complaining of a thick, pus-like discharge from his private part. Which infection is the most likely suspect?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Gonorrhoea
options.C: Primary syphilis
options.D: Genital herpes

explanation: Spot on! Gonorrhoea in men is classic for that heavy, purulent (pus-like) urethral discharge and burning when peeing.

question: Why does Graves' disease cause hyperthyroidism?

options.A: The pituitary gland stops releasing any regulatory hormones
options.B: Dietary iodine levels become excessively high in the bloodstream
options.C: Thyroid tissue undergoes widespread autoimmune destruction
options.D: Antibodies mimic TSH and continuously stimulate the thyroid gland

explanation: In Graves' disease, rogue antibodies trick the thyroid by acting just like TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone), forcing the gland to pump out way too much thyroid hormone.

question: What is the single best way to stop healthcare-associated infections in their tracks?

options.A: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.B: Wearing sterile gowns for all tasks
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics daily
options.D: Disinfecting room walls every shift

explanation: Spot on! Simply washing your hands thoroughly before and after touching a patient washes away germs picked up from the environment.

question: What are the three core components of the standard Post-Abortion Care (PAC) model?

options.A: Surgical sterilization, mandatory psychiatric evaluation, and legal reporting
options.B: Emergency treatment, family planning counseling, and reproductive health linkage
options.C: Antenatal booking, nutritional rehabilitation, and infant immunization
options.D: Blood transfusion, long-term hospitalization, and vocational training

explanation: PAC is a complete package: treat the immediate emergency, talk about family planning so it doesn't happen again, and connect the patient to ongoing health care. You'll see this model everywhere in public health!

question: What is the most crucial nursing check right after a neck biopsy or fine-needle aspiration?

options.A: Monitoring for signs of airway obstruction or bleeding
options.B: Checking for sudden spikes in fasting blood glucose
options.C: Testing the patient's 24-hour urine catecholamine levels
options.D: Encouraging immediate heavy physical exercise

explanation: Always protect the airway! Since the procedure is right in the neck near major blood vessels and the trachea, nurses must watch closely for swelling or bleeding.

question: Which tiny structures in the upper dermis are responsible for giving you your unique fingerprints?

options.A: Elastic fibers
options.B: Sweat glands
options.C: Dermal papillae
options.D: Subcutaneous fat

explanation: Well done! Dermal papillae are finger-like bumps that press up against the epidermis, creating those lovely ridges we know as fingerprints while helping supply nutrients.

question: What is the go-to treatment to quickly filter out dangerous levels of a heavy-duty poison like lithium?

options.A: Multiple-dose ipecac
options.B: Whole bowel irrigation
options.C: Hemodialysis
options.D: Gastric lavage

explanation: When the kidneys just can't keep up, hemodialysis steps in to act like an artificial kidney, filtering the dangerous drug straight out of the blood.

question: What is the very first thing you should do before making any hospital bed?

options.A: Strip all the old linens off the mattress simultaneously
options.B: Lock the bed wheels and adjust it to a comfortable working height
options.C: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the ward
options.D: Remove all pillows and place them on a nearby chair

explanation: Correct! Safety first: lock the wheels so the bed doesn't roll away, and raise it so you don't hurt your back while working.

question: What is the primary role of increased protein intake during the lactation period?

options.A: To provide quick energy during night feedings
options.B: To support tissue repair and milk synthesis
options.C: To maintain hydration and fluid balance
options.D: To prevent the baby from developing infant colic

explanation: Proteins supply the building blocks needed to create milk and help the mother's body heal from childbirth. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h3)

question: How do nurses commonly use mobile handheld devices in modern hospitals?

options.A: To scan patient ID bands and medication barcodes at the bedside
options.B: To play streaming music videos in patient rooms
options.C: To make personal phone calls during quiet night shifts
options.D: To take photographs of hospital visitors for security passes

explanation: Bedside scanners are a nurse's best friend for safety, helping ensure the right medication always reaches the right patient.

question: What do indirect health care costs mainly refer to?

options.A: Lost economic productivity and wages due to illness
options.B: The cost of ambulance fuel during emergency transport
options.C: Utility bills and building maintenance for the clinic
options.D: The price of surgical equipment bought by the facility

explanation: Indirect costs are about the money and work time lost when sickness keeps someone away from their job.

question: Why must you follow the manufacturer's recommended contact time for a disinfectant?

options.A: It allows the surface to dry completely without wiping
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing cleaning supplies
options.C: It ensures the chemical agent has enough time to kill pathogens
options.D: It prevents the disinfectant liquid from staining hospital furniture

explanation: You got it! Disinfectants aren't magic—they need a few minutes of wet contact time to actually break down and destroy stubborn germs on a surface.

question: How does chemoprophylaxis differ from standard immunization?

options.A: Chemoprophylaxis cures chronic illnesses, while immunization is only used for acute emergency surgeries.
options.B: Chemoprophylaxis creates lifelong immunity, whereas vaccines wear off after a single week.
options.C: Immunization is given to animals only, whereas chemoprophylaxis is exclusively reserved for human patients.
options.D: Chemoprophylaxis uses medications to prevent infection, whereas immunization uses antigens to stimulate antibody production.

explanation: You've got this! Chemoprophylaxis means using protective drugs (like malaria prevention tablets), while vaccines train your body's own immune system to fight back.

question: Why must management issue a query and hear a nurse's defense before taking disciplinary action?

options.A: To transfer the financial liability of the hospital to the nursing council
options.B: To ensure fairness, protect employee rights, and prevent arbitrary management actions
options.C: To delay disciplinary actions so that the offender can retire voluntarily
options.D: To allow the nurse to immediately apply for employment in another sector

explanation: Due process ensures everyone gets a fair hearing. Management cannot just punish you on a whim without letting you explain!

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when estimating injection commodity needs?

options.A: Performing regular physical inventory audits on the ward
options.B: Ignoring existing stock levels currently sitting in the storeroom
options.C: Collaborating closely with pharmacy and supply chain personnel
options.D: Reviewing past consumption reports from previous months

question: What is the basic function of the internet?

options.A: Printing out patient care plans automatically
options.B: Generating electrical power for medical machines
options.C: Connecting computers globally to share information instantly
options.D: Storing physical files inside a hospital filing cabinet

explanation: The internet is a global network designed primarily to link computers together so data can travel freely between them. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is a common traditional explanation often given for mental illness?

options.A: Regular physical exercise routines
options.B: A balanced and nutritious diet
options.C: Excessive intake of clean water
options.D: Spiritual attacks and witchcraft

question: How are blood-borne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B mainly spread during traditional FGM?

options.A: Exposure to contaminated air in rural communities
options.B: Drinking contaminated water after the procedure
options.C: Insect bites during outdoor healing rituals
options.D: Reusing unsterilized cutting instruments on multiple individuals

question: Which of these is a key administrative duty for a nursing unit manager?

options.A: Designing new blueprints for hospital buildings
options.B: Serving as the legal defense attorney for the hospital
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for the pharmacy
options.D: Conducting regular performance appraisals for ward staff

question: Why would a doctor order a 24-hour Holter monitor for a patient with occasional dizzy spells?

options.A: To continuously measure the oxygen saturation levels in the blood overnight
options.B: To deliver mild electrical shocks if the patient's heart rate drops too low
options.C: To catch intermittent dysrhythmias that do not happen during a quick clinic visit
options.D: To permanently replace the need for an invasive cardiac catheterization

explanation: Some heart flutters only happen once in a while. A 24-hour Holter monitor records the rhythm all day and night at home, helping catch those sneaky, unpredictable episodes!

question: What practical tool can a nurse recommend to help an elderly patient who forgets daily doses?

options.A: A strict fasting diet plan
options.B: A weekly pill organizer box
options.C: A large wall calendar for appointments
options.D: A daily rigorous exercise chart

question: How do residential care homes differ basically from nursing homes?

options.A: Nursing homes feature 24-hour medical staff for complex health needs, while residential care focuses on daily living assistance
options.B: Residential care homes are operated by the government, while nursing homes are private
options.C: Residential care homes are exclusively for children, whereas nursing homes are strictly for the elderly
options.D: Nursing homes do not provide meals, unlike standard residential care facilities

explanation: Spot on! The big difference is clinical staffing: nursing homes have 24-hour medical care for heavy health needs, while residential homes focus more on daily living support.

question: Who is considered a vital stakeholder in a nursing quality improvement project?

options.A: External auditors from the tax office
options.B: Only the hospital chief executive officer
options.C: Private security guards at the hospital gate
options.D: Frontline nurses, physicians, and patients

explanation: Spot on! Successful healthcare relies on teamwork. Everyone involved in giving or receiving care needs a seat at the table.

question: What is the main difference between congenital and acquired disabilities?

options.A: Acquired conditions never cause any emotional distress or grief
options.B: Congenital conditions are present from birth, while acquired ones happen later in life
options.C: Acquired conditions are always genetic and passed down in families
options.D: Congenital conditions only affect older adults in the community

question: Why is it important for a community nurse to understand disease agents?

options.A: To target specific causes when planning community disease prevention
options.B: To prescribe appropriate antibiotics without consulting a doctor
options.C: To accurately calculate hospital room bed turnover rates
options.D: To diagnose surgical complications before they become severe

explanation: When you know exactly what is causing an illness in your community, you can aim your prevention plans right at it and knock it out!

question: What is considered the most powerful tool for breaking down mental health stigma in communities?

options.A: Strict laws that fine people for speaking about mental illness
options.B: Personal contact and storytelling from people with lived experience
options.C: Locking away individuals who show signs of mental distress
options.D: Hiding psychiatric clinics behind high, secret walls

question: What are the three essential components required for valid informed consent?

options.A: Nurse supervision, police clearance, and legal representation
options.B: Capacity, adequate information, and voluntary agreement
options.C: Written signature, family approval, and hospital stamp
options.D: Doctor's orders, witness testimony, and full cash payment

question: Why do we let patients try out a new physical skill themselves during teaching?

options.A: It ensures the patient can safely perform the task on their own
options.B: It is required to update the electronic health record
options.C: It prevents the patient from asking difficult questions
options.D: It makes the nurse finish their shift much faster

explanation: Brilliant! Having them practice physically builds their confidence and proves they can handle it safely once they go home.

question: Which of the following is NOT a way to prepare for or prevent a disaster?

options.A: Ignoring safety regulations in industrial factories to save money
options.B: Stockpiling emergency medical supplies and personal protective gear
options.C: Conducting routine workplace evacuation drills with employees
options.D: Establishing strong communication links between local emergency agencies

explanation: Easy choice! Disregarding safety codes invites disaster rather than preparing for it.

question: Which type of study focuses on describing the person, place, and time of a disease outbreak?

options.A: Surgical audit
options.B: Analytical study
options.C: Clinical trial
options.D: Descriptive study

explanation: Correct! Descriptive studies simply paint the picture of who is sick, where they are, and when it happened. You're crushing it!

question: Which of these is an example of a strong system-level fix to prevent errors?

options.A: Redesigning automated medication dispensing cabinets to require double scans
options.B: Warning staff that future mistakes will result in immediate termination
options.C: Removing all safety policies to let nurses rely entirely on instinct
options.D: Telling nurses to pay closer attention so they never get tired

explanation: Brilliant! Changing technology and workflows creates a strong safety net that protects against human error much better than just telling staff to be careful.

question: What is the main goal of doing an endocrine stimulation test?

options.A: To cure the patient of chronic hormone overproduction
options.B: To check if a target gland can respond to a hormone
options.C: To remove antibodies attacking the endocrine tissues
options.D: To force the pituitary gland to shrink in size

explanation: We give a little push (a synthetic hormone) to see if a sleepy or struggling gland can wake up and respond like it's supposed to.

question: Which term covers both undernutrition and overnutrition?

options.A: Homeostasis
options.B: Anabolism
options.C: Metabolism
options.D: Malnutrition

explanation: Malnutrition isn't just about not having enough food—it's an umbrella term for any poor nutrition, whether someone is eating too little or too much.

question: Why is blunt heart injury often harder to spot right away compared to a stab wound?

options.A: X-ray machines cannot take pictures of blunt force trauma.
options.B: The chest wall often shows no open wounds or obvious external damage.
options.C: The heart stops beating completely right away.

question: What is the main purpose of infection control rules in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: To ensure that patients clean their own rooms after surgery
options.B: To establish clear standards that protect staff and patients from harm
options.C: To limit the purchase of expensive imported medical equipment
options.D: To reduce the number of nursing shifts required in each ward

explanation: Hospital policies are there to guide safe habits and keep everyone—both nurses and patients—free from avoidable infections.

question: Why do intestinal cells have to package dietary fats into structures called chylomicrons?

options.A: To convert fats directly into glucose

options.C: To allow transport into lymphatic lacteals
options.D: To make the fat molecules taste sweet

explanation: Fats are too bulky to slip directly into blood vessels, so enterocytes package them into chylomicrons so they can travel safely through the lymphatic vessels.

question: Why is strong social participation so helpful during a community health crisis?

options.A: Government officials will visit the town more often
options.B: Patients will no longer need to visit physical clinics
options.C: It automatically lowers the cost of imported medicines
options.D: Neighbors are more likely to cooperate and help each other

question: What happens when Nigeria falls short of the Abuja Declaration target for health spending?

options.A: Health institutions face severe underfunding and rely on alternative funding streams
options.B: Nurses receive higher salaries from international grants
options.C: International agencies take over total control of state clinics
options.D: Private hospitals are forced to close down permanently

explanation: When public health budgets fall short, hospitals struggle with basic running costs and have to look for other ways to survive.

question: Why did early birth control activists get into trouble with the law?

options.A: Laws classified reproductive health information as obscene and illegal

options.D: Pharmacists feared losing money on prescription medications

question: Which of the following is a key frontline responsibility of a reproductive health nurse?

options.A: Providing antenatal care and family planning counseling
options.B: Conducting biomedical laboratory research
options.C: Purchasing medical equipment for the entire hospital
options.D: Drafting national health insurance policies

question: What is the main role of a home care nurse when working with the healthcare team on a slow-healing wound?

options.A: Acting as the eyes and ears to report accurate, up-to-date wound changes to providers
options.B: Ordering all prescription medications without physician approval
options.C: Performing surgical debridement during every home visit

question: A patient with HIV can stay healthy and symptom-free for years. What is happening inside their body during this time?

options.A: The virus replicates slowly while the immune system gradually loses ground.
options.B: CD4+ cells are multiplying faster than the virus can destroy them.

question: What usually happens when a patient is discharged with a poor transition plan?

options.A: Instant recovery and permanent stability
options.B: Complete independence from all health services
options.C: Immediate employment in high-stress jobs
options.D: Rapid re-hospitalization or trouble with the law

question: Which of these best describes probability sampling?

options.C: Every member of the population has a known chance of being selected

explanation: Awesome! Probability sampling uses fairness and randomization, meaning nobody is unfairly favored and everyone has an equal shot at being picked.

question: A patient who had a leg amputation complains of severe pain in the toes of the missing foot. How should the nurse respond?

question: What is the main safety benefit of using high-tech simulation manikins in nursing school?

explanation: Simulation gives you a safe playground to make mistakes, learn from them, and master emergencies without risking human lives.

question: What is usually the very first sign a patient notices with oesophageal cancer?

options.B: Progressive difficulty swallowing solids
options.C: Severe burning pain right after eating
options.D: Uncontrollable hiccups lasting days

question: Why is the time right after breakfast often the best time to try having a bowel movement?

options.A: Stomach acid levels are at their lowest point of the day

options.C: Eating food triggers a natural wave of activity in the colon

question: As a nurse, why is it safest to use a drug's generic name during handovers and charting?

options.C: It remains universal and prevents medication errors caused by look-alike trade names

question: Why is proper waste management in a health facility considered a crucial part of infection control?

question: A nurse notices three patients on the same ward develop diarrhea within 24 hours. What is the best immediate action?

options.C: Wait until the end of the week to see if it stops

question: A 36-week pregnant mum asks why the nurse wants her to identify a blood donor and save transport money. How should the nurse reply?

question: What do not-for-profit health organizations do with any extra money they make?

options.A: Transfer it directly to government tax accounts

question: What is a major goal of public awareness campaigns in disaster management?
